name: The Suburbs
label: Twin/Tone
lede: Nine songs on red vinyl in 1978 started Twin/Tone, and sixteen years later a live album from the same band closed it.

eras.title: Art school kids, a red 7-inch
eras.text: Two Minneapolis suburbanites come home from Los Angeles art school, pick up three players from a band called the Tsetse Flies, and wind up on the first record Twin/Tone ever puts out.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Suburbs (band) · PopMatters: The Suburbs Celebrate Personal History
years.h: [[Chan Poling|ee72fe22-4355-48be-9a94-fd5093050d63]] and [[Beej Chaney|0376e2dc-f99e-4fdc-8a92-7de62c781095]] come home and start the Suburbs
years.p: The two had studied in Los Angeles; back in Minneapolis they teamed with drummer Hugo Klaers, guitarist Bruce C. Allen and bassist Michael Halliday.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the Suburbs to November 1977. Poling and Chaney had been in a Los Angeles band called the Technocats with Su Tissue of the Suburban Lawns, and Klaers, Allen and Halliday had been playing together as the Tsetse Flies.

Poling has said he studied contemporary classical music at CalArts but found punk and new wave more compelling. He credits Chris Osgood of the [[The Suicide Commandos|eb7988a4-4a66-4320-a6ea-d17da0da88ac]] with pointing the band toward Twin/Tone.

years.src: The Current: We started a scene · Wikipedia: The Suburbs (band)
years.h: Jay's Longhorn Bar hires a band that only plays originals
years.p: Owner Jay Berine hesitated over booking the Suburbs, then saw the crowds at their basement shows and made them regulars.
years.xp:
Klaers told The Current the basement parties drew 400 to 500 people, which persuaded Berine.

Klaers: "The Longhorn held 400 people, and the same 200 were there every night." Wikipedia adds that Bruce Springsteen, in town on the tour for The River, came to see the band and nearly joined them for an encore.

years.src: Diffuser: April 17, 1978: The Day the Suburbs Hit the Shelves · Wikipedia: The Suburbs EP · Twin/Tone: The Suburbs
years.h: The Suburbs EP is the first record Twin/Tone ever presses
years.p: Nine songs in about 16 minutes, on red vinyl, Twin/Tone catalog number TTR 7801.
years.xp:
The EP was cut at Blackberry Way in Minneapolis, produced by Twin/Tone co-founder Paul Stark. The label put out three EPs at once (Fingerprints, Spooks and the Suburbs), and the first pressing was 2,500 copies on red vinyl.

Peter Jesperson recalled the Longhorn's owner saying the band sounded like they had stepped right off the playground and onto the stage, which Jesperson thought would make a good slogan. Twin/Tone's own discography lists the release date as April 17, 1978.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bruce C. Allen · Wikipedia: Twin/Tone Records
years.h: Allen draws the Twin/Tone logo and the five-men-in-a-circle Suburbs mark
years.p: [[Bruce C. Allen|6e967a13-72e9-4af1-99d3-a9c87d139e84]] was the band's guitarist and its graphic designer, and the same hand did the label's branding.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Allen with the Suburbs logo, the Twin/Tone logo and art direction on the compilation Big Hits of Mid-America, Volume Three. Tiny Mix Tapes and Wikipedia also credit him with the cover of the [[The Replacements|dc0d05ce-2f47-4962-b4fa-8631a0a51987]] album Let It Be.

eras.title: The house band of Twin/Tone
eras.text: Three records and a run of dance singles on the label they helped launch, with a sound that moves from jittery new wave to double-album sprawl to club mixes.

years.h: "World War III" 7-inch, TTR 7909
years.p: The first single after the EP, with "Change Agent" on the B-side.

years.h: In Combo: the first full album
years.p: Paul Stark produced 31 minutes of debut album for Twin/Tone.
years.xp: AllMusic's Stewart Mason called it one of the pioneering releases of the American post-punk indie scene and, in his words, probably the band's greatest vinyl moment. Trouser Press's Ira Robbins heard signs of incipient musical greatness.

years.src: Wikipedia: Credit in Heaven · Twin/Tone: The Suburbs
years.h: Credit in Heaven: a double album with jazz, funk and disco in it
years.p: Seventeen songs, some near ten minutes, recorded April to June 1981 with Paul Stark.
years.xp:
Saxophonist Max Ray guests, and "Music for Boys" became a local radio hit. AllMusic's Mark Deming said it sometimes reaches beyond its grasp and is an under-appreciated milestone of Midwestern new wave. It won Best LP at the 1982 Minnesota Music Awards.

Sources disagree on the release date: Twin/Tone lists August 25, 1981; Wikipedia says September 25.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dream Hog EP · Twin/Tone: The Suburbs
years.h: "Waiting" goes out as a 12-inch, and the dance floors pick it up
years.p: The Dream Hog EP followed on November 30, produced by Steven Greenberg of Lipps Inc. and Paul Stark.
years.xp:
Greenberg had a hit with Lipps Inc.'s "Funkytown." Dream Hog's tracks include "Roll Over City" and "The Best Is Over," plus a club mix, and Twin/Tone released it as TTR 8230.

Greenberg then brought the band to Phonogram, and the EP was reissued on Mercury.

eras.title: Dinner jackets and major-label money
eras.text: Greenberg walks them to PolyGram, and for four years the Suburbs try to become what the Longhorn already thought they were.

q: We've always wanted to sell records, to join the big time.
years.h: Mercury reissues Dream Hog and the Suburbs leave Twin/Tone
years.p: Chan Poling told the press the band loved what Twin/Tone had done for them, but wanted to sell records.
years.xp: Producer Steven Greenberg introduced the band to Phonogram, which put Dream Hog out on Mercury as their first major-label release.

years.src: Wikipedia: Love Is the Law (Suburbs album) · The Suburbs: Bio
years.h: Love Is the Law comes out with a dead toreador on the cover
years.p: Recorded June and July 1983 with Greenberg and Paul Stark, and it won two Minnesota Music Awards.
years.xp:
The cover is Manet's painting The Dead Toreador; in Cashbox, Poling said the band liked the contrast of a warm title over a cold image. The album adds horns and a harder rock edge, with songs like "Perfect Communist" and "Monster Man." Trouser Press's Ira Robbins called it easily the band's apex.

The title song later became an anthem for the marriage equality movement, and the band's bio says as much. Wikipedia notes it was used on Roseanne, in Darlene's prom scene, in 1993.

years.h: "Rattle My Bones" is the band's other radio song
years.p: It later turned up in Target ads and became a Minnesota Vikings home-game staple.

years.h: Suburbs on A&M, produced by Prince's former drummer
years.p: Bobby Z. of the Revolution produced it, credited as "Robert Brent," at Metro Studios in Minneapolis.
years.xp: Reviews split. Stewart Mason of AllMusic said the production smothered what made the band good; Ira Robbins found it another powerful record, with less urgency than before. It was their only A&M album and was never issued on CD.

years.h: The Suburbs break up after a decade
years.p: MPR reported the band disbanded in 1987; the A&M record had not got the radio play the label wanted, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: Chaney goes west, the band reunites anyway
eras.text: A compilation, a reunion, a sitcom cameo and one last record for the label that started with them.

years.src: Wikipedia: Beej Chaney · The Current: Beej Chaney of The Suburbs has died
years.h: Beej Chaney moves to Los Angeles
years.p: The distance shaped the reunited band, according to Wikipedia; Chaney later bought a Malibu studio.
years.xp: Chaney released the EP Reckless Heart in 1992 and the album Windows in 2003. He bought Shangri-La, the Malibu studio, in the late 1990s and owned it until he sold it to Rick Rubin in 2011. The Current lists Weezer, Metallica, Kings of Leon and Mark Knopfler among those who recorded there.

years.h: Ladies and Gentlemen, The Suburbs Have Left the Building
years.p: Twin/Tone's best-of, catalog TTR 89232.

years.src: MPR News: Allen, guitarist for Suburbs, dies at 54 · The Current: The Suburbs announce first new album in 27 years
years.h: The Suburbs play together again
years.p: MPR News dates the first reunion to 1993; they kept doing a show or two a year.
years.xp: Chan Poling told The Current the band did one or two shows a year for two decades after the breakup.

years.src: Wikipedia: Twin/Tone Records · Twin/Tone: The Suburbs
years.h: Viva! Suburbs! Live at First Avenue: Twin/Tone's last record
years.p: The band that started the label also ends it: Wikipedia says the live album was Twin/Tone's final official release in 1994.
years.xp: Twin/Tone released over 300 records by roughly 100 bands over 17 years, per Wikipedia. The label was revived in 2017 for a Suicide Commandos album.

eras.title: Beejtar Records and a hard year
eras.text: Reissues on the band's own label, then the loss of the man who drew their logo.

years.h: Beejtar Records reissues In Combo, Credit in Heaven and Love Is the Law
years.p: The band put the three albums back out on CD on Chaney's label, followed by the 2003 best-of Chemistry Set: Songs of the Suburbs 1977–1987.

years.src: MPR News: Allen, guitarist for Suburbs, dies at 54 · Slicing Up Eyeballs: Bruce Allen of The Suburbs, 1955-2009 · The Current: The Suburbs announce first new album in 27 years
years.h: Bruce C. Allen dies at 54
years.p: MPR reported he died after being taken off life support following a week in hospital with internal bleeding.
years.xp:
Slicing Up Eyeballs reported that he had had organ failure, complications from triple bypass surgery the year before. Bassist Michael Halliday, who had arthritis, also stepped away that year.

Peter Jesperson: "They never made that big splash elsewhere, but locally they were like the Rolling Stones." Steve Brantseg and Steve Price joined for a benefit concert in Allen's honor.

eras.title: On their own money
eras.text: The band comes back on its own money, loses its co-founder and keeps playing.

years.src: MPR News: Chan Poling and The Suburbs use Kickstarter · Star Tribune: The 'Burbs are back · The Current: The Suburbs announce first new album in 27 years
years.h: Si Sauvage: the first new Suburbs album in 27 years
years.p: Backers on Kickstarter raised $73,000 for it, above a $65,000 goal.
years.xp:
Poling said going independent avoided the recoup trap of the 1980s, when a single video could cost $350,000. Rewards ran from a $10 download to a $10,000 private concert; two backers bought that one.

The band was Poling, Chaney, Klaers, Brantseg and Price with guests Janey Winterbauer and Aby Wolf. The Current has the release as August 27 and Wikipedia has November 19, so this page says only 2013.

years.src: PopMatters: The Suburbs Celebrate Personal History · Wikipedia: The Suburbs (band)
years.h: Hey Muse!, the first album without Chaney
years.p: Chaney took a leave of absence in August 2014, per Wikipedia; the band crowdfunded the record.
years.xp:
Poling told PopMatters the closing song, "When We Were Young," is the most literal thing he has written. He also said he is not going to get in a van and suffer for his art anymore.

Chaney's absence is stated inconsistently: Isthmus and PopMatters say he left; Wikipedia says leave of absence.

years.h: First band back at First Avenue after the pandemic closure
years.p: Two sold-out shows in the 7th Street Entry, tied to the album Poets Party.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Poets Party as their seventh studio album. The band has a star on First Avenue's exterior wall.

years.src: Star Tribune: Beej Chaney, Suburbs co-founder, dies · The Current: Beej Chaney of The Suburbs has died
years.h: Beej Chaney dies swimming near Hermosa Beach at 67
years.p: The Star Tribune reported officials ruled it an accident; he swam in the ocean daily.
years.xp:
He was finishing a rockabilly album with Robby Vee. Klaers told the Star Tribune: "There's not a guitarist in the world that plays a guitar like Beej."

The band's statement called him a true original who lived his art.

years.src: The Current: Interview: The Suburbs on A Pagan Ritual
years.h: A 1983 Cabooze show, recorded by Paul Stark, finally comes out
years.p: The Current covered the live album in May 2026 with the band in Minneapolis for shows.
years.xp: Poling said the Cabooze wasn't a place new wave bands usually played. Klaers said by then they were actually musicians traveling the country. Steve Price has been bassist since 2009.
